Problem 4 (Stigmergy and 'aligned'), the rules written before reading Moffett et al. 2021, Okhuysen and Bechky 2009 or any record. STIGMERGY. Options: (a) keep T4-007 with one member (T3-038); (b) withdraw it and place T3-038 in the D02 fourth-order theme that takes it; (c) return T3-041 and T3-060 where their records propose additions grounded in the work's state (the MP code); (d) any other option the sources and records show, named before it is weighed. Choose the option that (1) the members' records under each member theme support (the three codings of F-018 as they stand); (2) the organization-design source admits, Moffett et al. 2021 or Okhuysen and Bechky 2009, with Heylighen 2016 and Grasse 1959 only as the construct's own sources; (3) keeps D02 whole, every member theme in a fourth-order theme and every fourth-order theme grouping what it names; (4) serves the theory question (how a room coordinates many hands, how forms differ) and the method question (construction upward: a fourth-order theme groups its members, or says why not). On a tie, the option with fewer claims lacking support (the criterion's first item). The three-coder rule's outcome is not set aside by my belief alone. ALIGNED. 'The room aligned many hands' is said of the rooms whose own record reports the work it called for built (a report that the mark is up, done or finished, the completion element P11 after the calls P01), counted with its denominator; 'tried to align' is said of the rest. If fewer than half of the rooms carrying calls report the work built, 'tried' stays for the dimension as a whole and 'aligned' is said only of the counted rooms. The canvas is not evidence (rule 7); the members' reports in the record are. An adversarial reader may be asked for reasons on both sides; it decides nothing and is served no notes of mine.

Problem 4: an option named before it is weighed, as the rule logged first requires. (d) merge Stigmergy (T4-007, one member: T3-038, building and reporting the mark) with Standardization of output (T4-008, templates and coordinates) into one fourth-order theme named for Okhuysen and Bechky's coordination mechanism 'objects and representations' (2009, pp. 474-475: objects and representations 'coordinate by providing information' and 'offer a common referent around which people interact, align their work'; scaffolding, 'a representation that makes the progress of the task obvious'). Prompted by the reading of Okhuysen and Bechky 2009 (pp. 469, 474-475, 483) and Moffett et al. 2021 (Moffett and Garnier pp. 58-59; Warglien and Sartoris pp. 63-64; conclusions p. 71: for humans stigmergy is 'rare and invariably transitory', dependent on planning and standardization; in temporary organizations needs are made observable 'both by explicit signaling and by direct material observation'). Next: the declarations of T4-007, T4-008 and D02, their records, the mapping lines, then the weighing under the four rules.

Problem 4, 'aligned', under the rule logged first (c5c10_aligned.py): 370 of 705 rooms carry calls for hands (P01); 284 of them (0.768) carry a report that a work is up (P11), and in 233 (0.630) the first such report comes after the first call. By room size (items_in_window quartiles): 24 of 60 (0.400), 55 of 90 (0.611), 74 of 110 (0.673), 80 of 110 (0.727). More than half: 'the room aligned many hands' is said of the 233, with the count; 'tried to align' of the rest. What it rests on: Okhuysen and Bechky 2009 define coordination through what the definitions share, that people work collectively, the work is interdependent and 'a goal, task, or piece of work is achieved' (p. 469); the room's own report that the work is up is the record's evidence that the piece of work was achieved. It says nothing of who placed it (much of a room's artwork was placed by people who never wrote in it), and the canvas is not evidence. An adversarial reader was given c5c10_sparring_brief.md (declarations, member themes, the 72 three-coded records through cite.py, mapping lines, source line ranges, four options, the contract's questions; none of my notes) and runs read-only.

Problem 4, a count for the weighing (assignments_final, cited concepts): building and reporting the mark (T3-038) is carried by 237 rooms, the members of Standardization of output (T4-008) by 237, both by 89, either by 385. So 148 rooms report the state of their mark with no template or coordinates coded, and 148 share templates with no report coded. Option (d) would join two routes that split the rooms; the C3 mapping keeps them apart too (T4-007 information provision, T4-008 task division). D02's other information theme, Backstage decision-making (T4-010), holds planning in chats, not reports in the thread, so option (b) finds no theme that takes T3-038.
